paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Chayei Sarah 6 (printed Tanchuma): "'Your beginning small' is Abraham... yet at a hundred he fathered a son... h: "Whatever you can make shine, make shine"

p: — of what they said (Bereshit Rabbah, parashah 61):
— “‘And he sent them away from Isaac his son’—
— ‘Whatever you are able to make shine,
— so that you are not scorched
— that it refers to the eastern direction,
— that a remnant should remain of them
— “so that you are not scorched by Isaac’s coal”—
— that is, the fire of holiness,
— “A young Torah scholar who boils with anger—
— it is the Torah that makes him boil,
, — “and My words which I have placed in your mouth.”
— in the Introduction to Tikkunei Zohar:
— “And when it is taken from Gevurah,
— it is called the Oral Torah”

Rav Tzadok reads "shine" not as "go east" but as "give off light."

— to the land of the East,

— since they did not grasp the depth of his intent.
— And this is why the Midrash expounded
— about Isaac our father, peace be upon him,

— for from them Israel draws out

h: "Very": the good that comes out of its opposite

p: — And this is why it says “very,”
— in the manner of what is said:
— and behold, it was very good,”
— about everything that is the opposite of good,
, — that it too will be “very good.”
